title: John Simon's widow unhappy with RCMP apology for Wagmatcook shooting
article: WAGMATCOOK FIRST NATION, N.S. - John Simon's widow says an RCMP apology for shooting her husband is "garbage" and her family is going ahead with a lawsuit.

Chief Inspector Blair McKnight expressed "sympathy and condolences" to Patsy MacKay last Friday, the same day the RCMP Public Complaints Commissioner said the Mounties used "poor decision-making" in handling the December 2008 incident.
MacKay says the last two years have been "hell" for her family.
"I was very insulted by that (the apology)," she says. "I've been begging for a genuine apology for over two years and now that they're told to apologize they're going to."
Const. Jeremy Frenette shot Simon three times when responding to a domestic dispute call at man's house on the Wagmatcook First Nation, in Cape Breton.

The commission's report says Simon - whom police believed to be intoxicated and suicidal at the time of the shooting - pointed a rifle at the officer, but adds Frenette acted inappropriately and disobeyed orders not to enter the house.
The document also states RCMP managers did not properly coordinate its own internal examination of the incident.

"The Commission was unable to fairly assess the reasonableness of the RCMP decision to not launch disciplinary proceedings. The RCMP did not provide any records which demonstrated the matter was properly considered within the one-year limitation period."
A meeting between the Mounties, Simon's family and the Wagmatcook Band Council today turned out not to be a personal apology, but a discussion about a lawsuit.
Both Mackay and Simon's mother, Susie Bernard, are suing the RCMP for damages.
The meeting says Brian Arbuthnot - Wagmatcook's director of operations - has been on the books since before the commission released its findings.
